status: B5 Off-centre collage preferred by John on 7 October. G2 front selected. B4/B6 retained as alternatives; final artwork and production wrap pending.
method: Built-in image_gen reference-guided concepts. Printed snippets are generated interpretations of supplied actual page renders, not pixel-identical page composites. No interior export or gardening-data changes.
userDirection: Dark background to contrast with G2 and showcase snippets. Pieces must look torn from book pages and slightly angled, suggesting what is inside rather than explaining it. Explanation belongs on inside covers.

variants.name: Loose cluster
variants.variation: B4 — LOOSE CLUSTER. A spacious centred cream title and two-line subtitle in the top quarter. The middle, approximately y=28% to 68%, has a loose triangular cluster of THREE overlapping torn page fragments: broad Carrot heading/illustration corner sloping -7 degrees towards upper left, Kale calendar plus surrounding paragraph fragment sloping +8 degrees across lower left/centre, smaller tall Troubles scrap behind at right sloping +5 degrees. Mix portrait and landscape torn fragments; do not align them to a grid. The blurb is one neat left-aligned cream paragraph below the collage y=72% to 83%. Price and reserved panel on the bottom row. Editorial, warm, confident; moderate white-paper coverage with much green breathing room.
variants.prompt:
Use case: compositing / book-cover concept.
Make ONE finished flat BACK COVER, portrait 185:240 ratio, with the design filling the canvas. This is a design proposal for a contemporary UK gardening paperback, not a photograph of a whole book.
REFERENCES: image 1 is the SELECTED FRONT, only to match its cream, rich forest green, chunky rounded typography and bright orange/lime illustration character. DO NOT redraw or include the front cover. Image 2 is a REJECTED BACK; retain ONLY its deep forest green background and warm cream lettering, discard its grid, straight rectangular thumbnails, coloured edge bars and explanatory feel. Images 3, 4 and 5 are actual inside pages: Carrot, Kale, Carrot and Parsnip Troubles. Use them as the printed content on the paper fragments, with their distinctive actual title lettering, original vegetable drawings, small body text and colourful calendar dots faithfully retained as visual source.
NEW DIRECTION: A tactile editorial collage of pieces visibly TORN from these book pages. Each fragment is a partial page, with page context: some body text, a cut-off heading or column continuing out of the torn edge. Show a torn Carrot title/illustration page corner, a glimpse of a green growing-calendar inside a larger page scrap, and a smaller troubleshooting page fragment. Cream paper with fine irregular fibrous ripped edges, slight natural curl, subtle realistic contact shadows and overlapping layering. Rotate the fragments slightly in different directions, approximately 5–10 degrees. Their purpose is to entice with an impression of the contents, NOT to be readable explanatory diagrams. Do not isolate complete widgets in neat cards. Do not add captions, arrows, labels, tape, pins, scissors, dirt, botanical objects outside the printed fragments or unnecessary decorative elements. The pages should appear clean, modern and freshly torn, not aged parchment. Leave deep green visible between and around pieces. Print details may be partially occluded and intentionally cropped at torn edges.
ALL MAIN BACK-COVER COPY MUST BE CLEAR AND EXACT, separate from the paper collage:
Title: "The Vegetable Guru"
Subtitle: "44 growing guides and 14 troubleshooting guides" (smaller than the title, two lines allowed).
Placeholder blurb: "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat."
Bottom left price: "£17.50"
Bottom right a clean small white rectangular reserved panel, about 48 by 27 mm in cover proportions, labelled simply "ISBN / BARCODE". No invented number and no actual barcode.
Only the page fragments are angled. Main typography stays level. Maintain generous safe margins. Keep title, subtitle, blurb and barcode free of overlapping images. Deep forest green ground all the way to every edge; no cream border, no frame, no top/bottom multicolour bars, no website or UI. No author's name. Do not add the front-cover subtitle "Your at-a-glance growing companion" to this back.

B4 — LOOSE CLUSTER. A spacious centred cream title and two-line subtitle in the top quarter. The middle, approximately y=28% to 68%, has a loose triangular cluster of THREE overlapping torn page fragments: broad Carrot heading/illustration corner sloping -7 degrees towards upper left, Kale calendar plus surrounding paragraph fragment sloping +8 degrees across lower left/centre, smaller tall Troubles scrap behind at right sloping +5 degrees. Mix portrait and landscape torn fragments; do not align them to a grid. The blurb is one neat left-aligned cream paragraph below the collage y=72% to 83%. Price and reserved panel on the bottom row. Editorial, warm, confident; moderate white-paper coverage with much green breathing room.
variants.visualReview: Inspected full generated image: dark green ground, visible irregular paper tears, opposing slight rotations, layered page fragments, requested title/subtitle, lorem ipsum, GBP 17.50 and labelled blank ISBN/barcode panel. Main copy clear; deliberate cropping/occlusion limited to page fragments. Concept, not production art.

variants.name: Off-centre collage
variants.variation: B5 — OFF-CENTRE COLLAGE. Put the title at the upper left in two confident lines, with the subtitle underneath, using only the top 27% height. Below, a compact ragged-edged blurb column occupies the left 36% width from y=34% to 66%. The collage occupies the right 58% width, y=31% to 79%, and consists of THREE distinct angled overlapping pieces torn from the actual interior: a wide Carrot title and illustration tear upper-right tilted +7 degrees, a portrait torn page fragment with calendar and tiny body prose behind it tilted -8 degrees, and an irregular small Troubles drawing/text snippet low-right tilted +6 degrees. A few paper edges can approach the outer cover edge but not cross the safe text margins. Vary their scale and let the print feel incidentally glimpsed. Keep the bottom row clear for price left and the ISBN white panel right. Asymmetric, contemporary editorial cover, strong dark-green negative space.

variants.name: Paper sweep
variants.variation: B6 — PAPER SWEEP. Calm bold cream title across the top, subtitle below, both left aligned within generous margins. Place the lorem-ipsum blurb as a short full-width paragraph immediately BELOW the subtitle, around y=27% to 39%. Then create a striking wide irregular sweep of THREE torn interior-page pieces across the lower-middle (y=46% to 78%): one large half-width Carrot upper-page fragment at -6 degrees, a pale Kale page fragment behind at +9 degrees showing a partial calendar, and a narrower Troubles page sliver in the overlap at -4 degrees. The varied torn paper edges and subtle shadows should make the whole grouping look like physical pieces casually laid out. Show partial body paragraphs and broken page margins, not isolated rectangular panels. Keep room below for price left and ISBN panel right. Slightly more spare and graphic than the other variations, with a broad horizontal collage silhouette and no top grid.
